sentences: Umberto Boccioni painted this canvas, three metres wide, in 1910, and it is counted as his first major Futurist work.
Buildings under construction and factory chimneys appear along the top, but most of the picture is filled with men and horses fused in one violent effort.
At the centre a huge horse strains forward, dragging the men who try to hold it, a symbol of the energy and speed of the modern city.
The Futurists celebrated machines, labour and the fast-growing city, and here Boccioni traded the calmer suburban views of his earlier work for a swirling, charged surface.
Its original title was Il lavoro (Work), and it hung under that name at the Exhibition of Free Art in Milan in 1911.
The composer Ferruccio Busoni bought it in London in 1912, and the Museum of Modern Art acquired it from his son in 1951.
Boccioni himself died in 1916, aged thirty-three, after being thrown from his horse during cavalry training.
